2609.20593.title: WiC is Not WSD: A Study on LLMs and Lexical Ambiguity Resolution
2609.20593.paper_summary: Word-in-Context (WiC) remains challenging for language models, despite recent progress on lexical-semantic tasks. We hypothesise that this difficulty arises not only from comparing two contextual uses of a word, but also from the absence of an explicit sense inventory that specifies the relevant level of semantic granularity. We evaluate open LLMs on WiC and traditional Word Sense Disambiguation (WSD) under similar settings. We find that providing candidate senses, similar to what is done in traditional WSD, improves WiC performance in all settings. In general, explicit sense information helps models make more consistent and targeted judgements. Human evaluation further shows that many apparent WiC errors reflect label ambiguity or mismatches between model and annotator sense boundaries rather than simple failures of lexical understanding. In particular, results show that LLMs overthink the sense distinction often leading to errors based on overly fine-grained distinctions.
2609.20593.paper_summary_zh: Word-in-Context (WiC) 對於語言模型來說仍然具有挑戰性，儘管在詞彙語義任務上最近有所進展。<lb/>我們假設這一困難不僅來自於比較一個詞的兩種語境用法，還來自於缺乏明確的意義庫來指定相關的語義粒度水平。<lb/>我們在類似的設置下對開放的 LLM 進行 WiC 和傳統的詞義消歧 (WSD) 評估。<lb/>我們發現，提供候選意義，類似於傳統 WSD 中所做的，能在所有設置中提高 WiC 的表現。<lb/>一般來說，明確的意義信息幫助模型做出更一致和更具針對性的判斷。<lb/>人類評估進一步顯示，許多明顯的 WiC 錯誤反映了標籤模糊或模型與標註者之間的意義邊界不匹配，而不是簡單的詞彙理解失敗。<lb/>特別是，結果顯示 LLMs 過度思考意義區分，常常導致基於過於細緻的區分而產生錯誤。
